lens: Adversarial mod-stability review — Harmony/reflection update-fragility and save-corruption / uninstall safety, grounded in the Build 3672 decomp
verdict: Conditionally viable, but the plan materially understates two risks and must not ship Phase A as written. (1) The claim that "the GetData Postfix neutralises all ~15 unguarded call sites" is false: several sites call .HasTag(tag) on the SkillData, and EmployeeInstance.HasAnySkillWithTag uses `x?.HasTag(tag) ?? true` — a null/!cached SkillData is treated as HAVING EVERY TAG, and HasTag() on a runtime ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>() whose BuildTagCache() never ran (or threw) has undefined behaviour in an un-decompiled assembly. The Postfix returns a non-null object but does nothing to guarantee HasTag is safe on it. (2) The normal uninstall path is deleting the mod folder, which never runs OnUnloadAsync, leaving employees with a primary skill that has no SkillData — vanilla EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill, CompatibilityFixesEA03, JobDemandHelper and ScheduleHelper.GetEmployeeColor then NPE, and the employee cannot be fired through the crashing UI. That can brick a save. Proceed only with: a real kill-switch (role system degrades to Dormant + player-notified on any self-check failure), a data-layer uninstall repair that runs on onSaveGame/onNewDay rather than only on clean unload, hiring via a direct RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate action instead of mutating BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills, and Phase A shipped in isolation and left to survive one real game patch before B/C/D.
topIssues: GetData Postfix does NOT make custom skills safe. Grep of SkillHelper.GetData (Build 3672): EmployeeInstance.cs:230 and :235 HasAnySkillWithTag do `characterData.skills.Select(x=>SkillHelper.GetData(x.name)).Any(x => x?.HasTag(tag) ?? true)` — a missing SkillData is treated as HAVING the tag. Callers: EmployeeInstance.cs:766/779/835 and ScheduleHelper.cs:233 recompute security every hour on TagRef.Skilltag.affectssecurity. In the inject-gap window our managers silently 'affect security' (score desync); worse, once the Postfix returns our runtime instance, HasTag() runs on an instance whose BuildTagCache() we called in try/catch — if it threw, HasTag can throw and crash the hourly security pass. TaggedScriptableObject/BuildTagCache/HasTag are in an un-decompiled assembly, so this is unknown until tested.

CompatibilityFixesEA03 runs unguarded over every employee AND candidate on every save load. EnsureAllFullTimeEmployeesHaveFullTimeDemand.cs:14 `skills.Any(x => SkillHelper.GetData(x).HasTag(TagRef.Skilltag.forcefulltime))` — no null guard, Skill-overload. EnablePartAndFullTimeToRecruitmentCampaigns.cs:13 `GetData(campaign.skillRequirement.skillName).HasTag(...)` — fires if the player has an active recruitment campaign for the mod skill. SaveGameManager.TryPrepareLoad runs AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll() (synchronous, WaitForCompletion) BEFORE InitializeLoadedSave() -> SaveGameCompatibilityFixes.ApplyCompatibilityFixes, so the OnSkillDataLoaded Postfix does fire first — but ONLY if the Harmony patch applied. If it silently failed to apply (signature drift, Harmony version clash), every load with one mod-skill employee hired throws inside the compat-fix runner, which can abort the load.

Mutating BusinessType('ba:businesstype_headquarters').employeePrimarySkills has side effects the plan ignores. That array is not just the Recruitment-Agency dropdown source (RecruitmentSettings.cs:100 intersects it with availableEmployeeSkills): it is also the AI staffing pool (Helpers/BusinessEmployeeGenerator.cs:47, RivalDefenseHelper.cs:162 SelectMany over rival ownedBusinesses' employeePrimarySkills) and the office simulation selector (OfficeBusinessSimulator.cs:46 `skills.First(x => businessType.employeePrimarySkills.Contains(x.name))` — .First(), throws if unmatched). If AI rivals own HQ registrations, appending our skill drags the fragile custom skill into AI employee generation and AiBusinessEmployeeData.cs:98 `SkillHelper.GetData(primarySkillName)`.

Folder-delete uninstall bricks saves. OnUnloadAsync only runs on a clean in-game mod unload; the common uninstall is deleting the mod directory, after which the save still contains EmployeeInstance.characterData.skills[0].name = 'sm:skill_storemanager' with no SkillData. Vanilla NPEs: EmployeeHelper.cs:353/361 CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(.baseHourlyWage), :452 GetTrainingCost, JobDemandHelper.cs:124/142, ScheduleHelper.cs:142 associatedColorGradient.EvaluateRandom, CompatibilityFixesEA03, plus MyEmployees rendering. Employee is effectively unfireable through the crashing UI. Not in the plan's risk list at the right severity.

BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs patch is the single most fragile Harmony surface and the lowest-value. Confirmed Build 3672: SetUpTabs is a private void in the GLOBAL namespace, _tabs/menu/containers are private [SerializeField], the HQ tab-id list is hardcoded (line 224-230), and the trailing loop `foreach (Transform item in menu) item.gameObject.SetActive(_tabs.Contains(item.name))` hides anything not in _tabs. SetTab.cs:309 does `_currentTabText = menu.Find(tabName).GetComponent<TextMeshProUGUI>()` then line 310 `_currentTabText.color = ...` — GetComponent, NOT GetComponentInChildren, so if the cloned PurchasingAgents button carries its label on a child, clicking our tab NPEs every time. The BizMan UI is refactored frequently by the devs.

SkillLegacyMap proves the skill system is under active migration and is a top 'breaks on a patch' vector the plan omits. BigAmbitions.SaveSystem.Legacy.SkillLegacyMap rewrites skill-name strings across ~28 save fields on load (Skill.name, SkillData.skillName, BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills, Item.suitableSkills, RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills, AiBusinessEmployeeData.primarySkillName, BuildingRegistration.uniformsBySkill.key, RecruitmentAgencyTargets.skillNameTarget, EmployeePreset.skill, ...). Today it is int-enum -> string only, so our string passes through. A future build adding a string normalization pass that drops unknown skill names would silently wipe every mod-skill employee's primary skill -> the vanilla NPE cascade above, on load, with no mod code able to intervene.

Reflecting the private static readonly SkillHelper.Skills dictionary by field name is avoidable fragility. A field rename breaks the primary injection and leaves only the GetData Postfix (which cannot help the HasTag paths). A Prefix on the public OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData> skillData) that adds our SkillData objects to the incoming list before the game copies it into the dict uses only the public method signature — no private-field reflection — and rides the same wipe-and-rebuild cycle.

associatedColorGradient path: ScheduleHelper.cs:142 calls `.associatedColorGradient.EvaluateRandom(employeeId.GetHashCode())`, not Evaluate() as the research states. A `new Gradient()` with only colorKeys set but no alphaKeys (or vice versa), or the EvaluateRandom extension's own assumptions, may throw or return default. Needs both colorKeys and alphaKeys populated and an in-game check of EvaluateRandom specifically.

My Employees job title rendering is assumed, not verified. EmployeeCellView.cs:59 sets `primarySkill.Arguments = new { skillName = data.primarySkillName, percentage = ... }` on a TextLocalizationComponent. Whether the loc template resolves `{skillName}` as a nested localization key (giving 'Store Manager') or interpolates the raw string (giving the literal 'sm:skill_storemanager') depends on the template — the plan's D-section claim that 'the loc key IS the skill id verbatim' is unconfirmed against Build 3672.

Harmony version sharing: ModAssemblyLoader caches by simple assembly name, so two mods bundling different 0Harmony majors share whichever loads first. The plan notes this but still bundles 0Harmony and assumes 2.3.x semantics; a co-installed mod with an older Harmony can change Patch() return values and AccessTools behaviour under our feet.
recommendedChanges: Add a real kill-switch: one static RoleSystemState { Active, DegradedPanelOnly, Dormant }. At init run an ordered self-check gauntlet, each step wrapped: (a) GameVersion.buildNumber in window; (b) every reflection/AccessTools handle non-null; (c) build a probe SkillData, BuildTagCache() in try/catch, then ASSERT HasTag(anyKnownTag) does not throw and that a forced OnSkillDataLoaded re-run leaves GetData returning the probe; (d) all harmony.Patch() calls return non-null. First failure drops to the lowest safe state, logs ONE Notifications.Show + ONE EnsurePermanentContact phone message. Dormant = inject no skill, mutate no array, allow no hire; existing modData plans load read-only, ManagerDirectory stops writing DeliveryContracts, weekly planner no-ops, panel shows 'Store Manager role disabled on this game build — supervision paused, no data lost.'

Move uninstall repair to the data layer. Every time a manager is created/hired, persist `sm.employeeFallback.v1 : { employeeId: originalPrimarySkillName }` into GameInstance.modData. On GlobalEvents.onSaveGame AND onNewDay, if RoleSystemState != Active OR the skill failed to inject this session, immediately re-skill any employee whose primary is sm:skill_* back to the recorded fallback (or ba:skill_purchasingagent). Do not rely on OnUnloadAsync. Ship a console command StoreManager.SafeRemove that re-skills all mod employees, strips the modData role blobs, and prints 'safe to delete the mod folder now' — document this as THE uninstall procedure in the mod README and the ModOptions panel.

Decide the primary-vs-secondary skill question with the folder-delete failure mode explicit, and gate it on in-game test. If deleting the mod folder with one hired manager prevents the save loading in vanilla, ship the manager as skills[0] = ba:skill_purchasingagent (vanilla-safe primary, keeps GetPrimarySkill()/wage/schedule working) + skills[1] = sm:skill_storemanager for the mod's own role logic, and drive the plan off HasSkill('sm:skill_storemanager') not GetPrimarySkill(). Accept that My Employees then shows 'Purchasing Agent' as the title. Only use a mod-skill PRIMARY if the test shows vanilla tolerates it.

Inject via a Prefix on the public SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData>) that adds the mod SkillData objects to the incoming list, instead of reflecting the private Skills field. Keep the [ModEntryOnCityLoad] backstop, but have it call OnSkillDataLoaded again with the current list + ours rather than touching the dict directly. Keep both GetData Postfixes purely as defence-in-depth.

For Phase A, hire via a direct mod action calling Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate('sm:skill_storemanager', 20f, hqAddress, null, 0f) -> normal Candidates -> HireCandidate flow. Do NOT mutate BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills in v1 (it feeds AI staffing, OfficeBusinessSimulator.First(), rival defense). Revisit agency-dropdown integration (which does require both employeePrimarySkills and availableEmployeeSkills) as a later opt-in once AI-pool contamination is ruled out by test #7.

Cut the HQ BizMan tab (Phase B) from v1 entirely. It is the highest-fragility patch (private SetUpTabs, blind prefab clone, SetTab GetComponent<TMP> assumption) for zero new capability — the ModOptions panel already drives every ManagerDirectory action. Ship the panel as the only UI until Phase A survives a real game patch.

Harden every SkillData field the decomp shows consumed unconditionally: skillName + name set; baseHourlyWage; trainingCostMultiplier = 1; secondarySkill = string.Empty (kills HeadhunterPlan.cs:108 and GenerateCandidate secondary branch); secondarySkillRange = new Vector2Int(5,20); possibleDealbreakers = new List<string>() (non-null — HeadhunterPlan enumerates it); associatedColorGradient = new Gradient() with BOTH colorKeys AND alphaKeys set (ScheduleHelper.cs:142 EvaluateRandom); icon28 = null is tolerated. Call BuildTagCache() in try/catch and treat any throw as self-check failure (c) -> Dormant.

Pin the build-number gate to the actual tested build with a narrow ceiling (e.g. [3672, 3699]) not [3600,3899]; every point release in that window is unverified. Widen it only after re-testing on a new build. On buildNumber outside the window -> DegradedPanelOnly at most, never Active.

Add explicit over-capacity tolerance to Reconcile now (not Phase D): HQ desk/sqm capacity is read live, so a player mid-remodel can drop below current assignments — Reconcile must freeze new assigns and never auto-drop or auto-fire.

Log a single structured line at each lifecycle point (init patched, OnSkillDataLoaded prefix fired, city-load backstop fired, compat-fix pass observed) so the ordering assumptions can be confirmed from Player.log without a debugger, and so a future-build regression is diagnosable from a user's log paste.
v1ScopeRecommendation: Ship Phase A only, in isolation, and let it survive one real Big Ambitions patch before starting B/C/D. Within Phase A, narrow further: (1) skill injection via a Prefix on the public OnSkillDataLoaded (no private-field reflection) + both GetData Postfixes as defence-in-depth; (2) hire via a direct RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate mod action — do NOT touch BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills / RecruitmentAgencySettings / HQ desk suitableSkills in v1; (3) manager stored as secondary skill on a vanilla primary unless in-game test proves a mod-skill primary is vanilla-safe on folder-delete; (4) ModOptions panel stays the only UI — no HQ BizMan tab; (5) full kill-switch (Active/DegradedPanelOnly/Dormant) and onSaveGame/onNewDay data-layer uninstall repair are part of Phase A, not deferred. Defer entirely: HQ BizMan tabs (B), Team Leader + the second custom skill + departments + merge/trim approval math (C), Assistant Manager (D). The core user value — weekly supervised DeliveryContract restock — is already delivered by v2's logic; re-parenting it onto one custom Store Manager skill is the whole v1. Team Leader/departments multiply the mod-arbitrated compounding-math surface (the D12 trap) and add a second fragile skill without touching that core value.
mustVerifyInGameFirst: SkillData.BuildTagCache() on a ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>(): does it throw? Then does HasTag(any TagRef.Skilltag value) on that instance return false rather than throw? Then hire/fake an employee holding ONLY the mod skill and call HasAnySkillWithTag(TagRef.Skilltag.affectssecurity) — confirm no exception in the hourly security pass (EmployeeInstance.cs:766/779/835, ScheduleHelper.cs:233).

Does the Harmony patch on SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded actually apply and fire on all of: new game, load save, city change? Add a log line in the patch and one in a patch on SaveGameCompatibilityFixes.ApplyCompatibilityFixes; confirm the skill patch fires first every time (decomp says TryPrepareLoad -> RegisterAndLoadAll precedes InitializeLoadedSave, but verify at runtime).

Uninstall by deleting the mod folder with 1 hired Store Manager on a test save: does the save still load in fully vanilla Build 3672? Enumerate every NPE (wage calc, training cost, JobDemandHelper, ScheduleHelper.GetEmployeeColor, CompatibilityFixesEA03, MyEmployees UI). This single test decides whether the secondary-skill model is mandatory.

My Employees + candidate card: set primarySkill.Arguments.skillName = 'sm:skill_storemanager' with Locales/en.json containing that key — does the row render the localized 'Store Manager' (template resolves nested key) or the literal id string? Check the loc template used for existing skill rows.

Actual wage: CalculateHourlyWageForSkill('sm:skill_storemanager', 20f) output vs the ~$30 target; read vanilla ba:skill_purchasingagent.baseHourlyWage and ba:skill_customerservice.baseHourlyWage in the same session for calibration (StoreManager.DumpSkill).

Does ba:businesstype_headquarters run OfficeBusinessSimulator or any per-hour simulation that calls skills.First(x => employeePrimarySkills.Contains(x.name)) over scheduled staff? If yes, a scheduled manager without a matching primary-skill entry throws — appending to employeePrimarySkills becomes mandatory, changing the risk calculus.

Do AI rivals own ba:businesstype_headquarters registrations (RivalDefenseHelper.cs:162, BusinessEmployeeGenerator.cs:47)? Determines whether appending our skill to HQ employeePrimarySkills contaminates AI employee generation and AiBusinessEmployeeData.cs:98.
RecruitmentAgencySettings: is availableEmployeeSkills one shared Addressable asset instance or per-building copies, and does a mutation survive a city load / save reload within the same session?

Headhunter: select the mod skill in the headhunter dropdown (HeadhuntersRecruitingTab iterates SkillHelper.AllSkillNames) and run a headhunter plan — confirm HeadhunterPlan.cs:74/108/138 and HeadhunterHelper.cs:100 survive with the injected SkillData and a tag-cache-built instance.

If Phase B is ever attempted: clone the live PurchasingAgents BizMan menu button and confirm menu.Find(id).GetComponent<TextMeshProUGUI>() resolves non-null (SetTab.cs:309-310), and that inserting the id into the private _tabs list keeps the user from being kicked off the tab (BizManBusiness.cs:166-168).
